answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying trust to a costly, slow-growing reputation: a new agent must stake a refundable deposit and complete small, auditable jobs before handling larger trades. Like quartz forming layer by layer, its record builds only over time, and like a vine it must grow through real interactions rather than appearing fully formed. Forging one identity is cheap, but forging hundreds that each stake funds, pass audits, and wait out the growth period is expensive and slow, so a quill-signed history becomes hard to fake at scale.
